Subject: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention/deletion

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope an accurate security attachment for the SOW.

Recap (short):
- Demo covered model routing, private VPC option, and our Console controls for policy-driven routing and auditing.
- You flagged two compliance priorities: (1) retention and deletion SLAs (including backups) and (2) SOC 2 / HIPAA readiness for a potential BAA.

Questions for your team (so we can draft the right language):
1) Retention target: What retention window do you need for primary data and logs (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days)?
2) Backups: Do you require guaranteed deletion from backups within the same SLA window, or do you accept a defined backup retention policy and legal-hold exceptions?
3) Deletion scope: Should deletion include KV cache, snapshots, and any exported logs (e.g., system-level logs retained for debugging)?

Attachments: I’ve attached our SOC 2 summary and a short data-retention matrix that maps retention tiers to parts of the stack (primary store, logs, backups).

Next steps we propose:
- Marissa (CC) to kick off a short security Q&A doc with your security team and propose optional wording for deletion/backups.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security/ops team next week to walk the Q&A.

Please reply with the retention window and whether deletion must apply to immutable backup snapshots. If you prefer, we can also start the questionnaire and share edits in Drive.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the fit assessment.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Couple of clarifications from our side before the Q&A: 

1) Primary retention: Our baseline is 90 days for transaction-level data; logs should be available for 180 days unless stricter rules apply.
2) Backups: We need clarity on whether deletion requests will cascade to backups. For regulated data (PHI), we typically require deletion from all copies within a defined SLA unless there's a legal hold.
3) HIPAA / BAA: Do you offer a BAA? If yes, what's your timeline for executing one (and is it a standard addendum or a bespoke agreement)?

Also — we’ve got a security engineer (security@ccs-healthcare.com) who will take the lead on the questionnaire. Please put Marissa in touch with them.

If you can confirm SOC 2 Type II status and give a short note on backup retention mechanics, that will help us draft an initial SOW.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, IT Security — CCS Healthcare

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention/deletion

Alex — looping in answers here and proposed next steps. Short answers up front: SOC 2 Type II completed (report summary attached), and we do support a BAA. Longer details below.

SOC 2 / BAA
- Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II covering infrastructure, change management, and logical access for our hosted offering (report summary = redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf).
- We can execute our standard BAA; timing is typically 7–14 business days once contracts are in legal review. If any bespoke language is needed, add an approximate 2-week negotiation window.

Retention / Deletion (how it works today)
- Default retention tiers: primary data (write-optimized store) = configurable, defaults to 90 days; application/system logs = 180 days; backups (snapshots) = 30 days rolling by default.
- Backups are retained as immutable snapshots on object storage for disaster recovery. Deleting PII from immutable backups is operationally complex — our standard approach is:
  * For standard deletion requests, we purge primary data and logs within the agreed SLA.
  * For backups, we provide documented backup-rotation windows (e.g., 30 days) and can offer shortened backup retention as a contract option (e.g., 7/14/30 days) for an additional data-management fee.
  * For legal-hold scenarios, we suspend deletion during the hold and flag affected records.

Deletion scope (what we can include in the SLA)
- Included by default: primary store, application logs, and KV cache eviction.
- Optional / negotiated: faster backup rotation, explicit snapshot scrub (subject to technical constraints and testing), and certified deletion attestations.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I will create and share a security Q&A doc (ccs-mrp-qna.docx) with questions on tokens, PII fields, export patterns, and legal-hold workflows — please ask your security team to populate it.
2) If CCS confirms a desired backup retention window (7 / 14 / 30 / 90 days), we’ll draft SOW language that maps to the pricing appendix.
3) Offer a 30-minute technical session next Thursday to walk through our backup mechanics and deletion test plan.

If you want an itemized cost for a shortened backup window and a certified deletion attestation, let me know and I’ll loop in pricing.

Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
